abstract: Chinese Hamster Ovary (CHO) cells dominate biotherapeutic manufacturing but still have a few limitations in post-translational modifications such as N-glycan branching, O-glycan core extension and inefficient protein folding/processing. It is yet unclear whether these CHO-specific traits reflect general Chinese hamster biology or arise specifically from cell line immortalization. We assembled a uniformly processed transcriptome compendium of 350 RNA-seq samples from 24 studies, integrating nine native Chinese hamster tissues with four CHO lineages (CHO-K1, CHO-S, CHO-DG44, CHO-DXB11). While CHO cells retain core proliferative and biosynthetic machinery when compared to Hamster tissues, it has undergone coordinated and selective loss of tissue-specific functions, and thus establishing these are immortalization-driven traits rather than general hamster-biology origin. Focused analysis of CHO cell lines further revealed that parental lineage and culture media as the dominant drivers of observed transcriptional heterogeneity where the cell identity is responsible for transcriptome variation in a higher proportion of genes. By integrating genome copy number or alternate promoter usage with gene expression data, we observed that while gene copy number variations contributions are almost negligible, alternate promoter usage governs the variation in about 20% of genes that showed cell line specific patterns while 60% had a buffering effect, indicating that additional, yet to be characterized regulatory layers drive CHO cell heterogeneity. Together, these findings establish a genomic and regulatory framework for understanding CHO lineage divergence, with direct implications for rational cell line selection and engineering in biotherapeutic manufacturing.
